\cvsection{Professional Summary}
Computational physicist with a PhD in Physics and ten years of experience building and running simulation codes for relativistic plasmas. Author of Paramo, an open-source Fortran library that solves the Fokker-Planck equation coupled to radiative transfer. Led an upgrade of the PatchworkMHD code on Frontera and used gradient-based optimization to calibrate model parameters against observations. Nine publications and a NASA grant won and led as a postdoc.\par

\cvsection{Skills}
\textbf{Simulation:} Kinetic plasma modeling (Fokker–Planck), radiative processes (synchrotron, inverse Compton), radiative transfer, relativistic MHD, Lagrangian particle dynamics, numerical PDEs, finite-difference/finite-volume methods, numerical linear algebra, parameter estimation, uncertainty quantification\par
\textbf{HPC \& Parallel:} OpenMP, OpenACC (GPU offloading), MPI, SLURM, PBS, HDF5\par
\textbf{ML \& Data:} Scientific ML, PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Astropy, random forest, SVM, neural networks, gradient-based optimization, parameter estimation\par
\textbf{Languages:} Python, C/C++, Fortran, Rust, R, SQL, Java, Julia, Shell\par
\textbf{Tools:} Git, Docker, Jenkins, QGIS, ParaView, VisIt\par

\cvsection{Projects}
\leftright{\textbf{Blazar Population ML}}{Jan 2026 – Present}\nopagebreak
\leftright{\textit{Scientific ML (Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch)}}{\href{https://github.com/altjerue/ilwikak-ml}{github.com/altjerue/ilwikak-ml}}\nopagebreak
